newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing fines China Securities, bans underwriting.
newsitem.headline: Beijing fines China Securities, bans underwriting.

text.p: The China Securities Regulatory Commission has fined China Securities, one of the country's top brokerages, two million yuan and suspended it from underwriting for two months from July 5 for irregularities, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.

The commission, China's top securities watchdog, also fined Shengli Oil Field Daming Group Co, one million yuan for an illegal share split, the newspaper said. Shengli is an A share company listed on the Shenzhen stock exchange.

The paper said an investigation by the commission found that, before its share issue and listing in June this year, Shengli Daming illegally split its shares and deliberately concealed this fact in its prospectus and listing statement.
China Securities knew of the share split but helped the company hide the fact, the paper quoted a commission statement as saying.
The securities watchdog ordered the two companies to reveal the responsible persons and report them, it said.
The commission also fined the legal firm and accounting firm involved in the listing, the newspaper said.
